source_text: Originale autem peccatum, si generatione primae nativitatis attrahitur, nuptias quidem a Deo institutas damnare potest, ceterum auferri a parvulis non potest; quoniam quod innascitur, usque ad finem eius, cui a principiorum causis inhaeserit, perseverat.
pass_a_gloss: But original sin, if it is drawn by the generation of the first nativity, can indeed condemn marriages instituted by God, but for the rest it cannot be taken away from little ones; since what is inborn perseveres until the end of him to whom it shall have clung from the causes of beginnings.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: But if original sin is contracted through the generation of the first birth, it may indeed condemn marriage, which God established, but it cannot be removed from infants. For something inborn remains until the end of the being to which it has belonged from its originating causes.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
